QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.claim: When Moses connects with the fire, he is called beyond fiery curtains of majesty; “I am your Lord” is God's manifestation veiled in a fiery form.
QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.anchor: أي: اتصل بها { نودي } من وراء

FARRA:v2p175/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r3.claim: With the call addressed to Moses, إني أنا ربك begins with kasra; the readings also allow the call to encompass أني and موسى.
FARRA:v2p175/r3.anchor: إن جعلت النداء واقعا على (موسى) كسرت (إني أنا ربك)

NAHHAS:v3p33/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p33/r5.claim: نودي means “he was told,” which explains the variant readings of يا موسى أني.

NAHHAS:v3p33/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r6.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v3p33/r6.claim: They read أني with fatḥa, meaning “he was called that I am”; أن is accusative.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r6.anchor: قرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو ( نودي يا موسى أني ) بفتح الهمزة بمعنى نودي بأني

NAHHAS:v3p33/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p33/r7.claim: Readers who give the hamza kasra understand Moses as saying “I am.”
NAHHAS:v3p33/r7.anchor: ومن كسر فالمعنى عنده قال إني

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.claim: On the preceding question about divine istiwāʾ, the author says the sounder view of Abū ʿAlī is that it means power; the Kullābī account of an act or attribute called istiwāʾ is unintelligible.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.anchor: وإن كان الأصح ما ذهب إليه أبو علي أن المراد به الاقتدار

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r3.claim: They read “annī” with fatḥa, understood as “because I am your Lord”; the others use kasra as the beginning of a new quotation, “he said: I am.”
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو: ياموسى أني أنا ربك بفتح الألف

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r4.claim: These readers open the final yāʾ in “innī”; the remaining readers leave it quiescent.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r4.anchor: فأما الياء ففتحها أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

MUQATIL:20:9-12/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:9-12/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:9-12/r2.claim: At the valley Tuwa, God calls Moses and orders him to remove sandals made from the skin of an unritually dead donkey; Tuwa is the valley’s name and means the purified valley.

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas describes a green tree glowing white from bottom to top like fire, with neither the flame changing its greenness nor the tree’s moisture dimming the flame; Moses saw great light and heard angels glorifying God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس رأى شجرة خضراء من أسفلها إلى أعلاها كأنها نار بيضاء

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r13.speaker: وهب
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r13.claim: Wahb narrates that Moses approached the apparent fire with dry sticks; it moved toward him, retreated, repeatedly tempted him, then vanished, while the branch glowed skyward and a dazzling light appeared.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r13.anchor: قال وهب : فظن موسى عليه السلام أنها نار أوقدت فأخذ من دقاق الحطب ليقتبس من لهبها

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r16.claim: The immediate-sequence particle faʾ does not exclude a brief interval between Moses’ arrival and the call.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r16.anchor: تخلل الزمان القليل فيما بين المجيء والنداء لا يقدح في فاء التعقيب

ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r5.claim: With fatḥa on أني, the sense is ‘he was called by the words that I am your Lord,’ and أني is accusative.
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r5.anchor:
فمن قرأ " أني " فالمعنى نودي بأني أنا
ربك، وموضع " أني " نصب.

ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r6.claim: With kasra on إني, the call is ‘O Moses, I am your Lord.’
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ (إني أنا ربك) بالكسر فالمعنى نودي يا موسى إني أنا ربك.

TABRISI:20:9-16/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
TABRISI:20:9-16/r1.claim: These readers open the initial alif in anī anā rabbuka; the remaining readers pronounce it with kasra.
TABRISI:20:9-16/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو أني أنا ربك بفتح الألف والباقون إني بالكسر

TABRISI:20:9-16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:20:9-16/r6.claim: The kasra treats the speech as direct quotation after Moses is called; the fatḥa connects it to what he was called with, since calling may take a preposition.
TABRISI:20:9-16/r6.anchor: من كسر إني فلأن الكلام حكاية كأنه نودي فقيل يا موسى إني أنا ربك ومن فتح

TABRISI:20:9-16/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16/r7.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:20:9-16/r7.claim: For passive nūdiya, a clause cannot serve as the passive subject; an implicit pronoun must do so, or Moses can be the subject because he was already mentioned.
TABRISI:20:9-16/r7.anchor: وينبغي أن يكون في نودي ضمير يقوم مقام الفاعل لأنه لا يجوز أن يقوم واحد من قوله يا موسى

TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.claim: As Moses approached, the fire appeared in a jujube tree; its brilliant light and vivid green amazed him before the tree called him.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.anchor: فإذا النار في شجرة عناب فوقف متعجبا من حسن ضوء تلك النار وشدة خضرة تلك الشجرة

TABRISI:20:9-12/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r10.speaker: وهب
TABRISI:20:9-12/r10.claim: Wahb reports that Moses heard a call from the tree, answered that he heard a voice but could not see its place, and learned by the response and a miracle that the caller was his Lord.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r10.anchor: نودي من الشجرة فقيل يا موسى فأجاب سريعا ما يدري من دعاه فقال إني أسمع صوتك ولا أرى مكانك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r7.claim: When Moses reached it, he reached what he had thought was fire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r2.claim: The majority read innī with kasra, supplying a speech verb or treating the call as speech; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read wa-annī with fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إني بكسر الهمزة على إضمار القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r3.claim: Moses knew the speaker through divinely created knowledge or a miracle; Muʿtazilites require miraculous proof and reject necessary knowledge as incompatible with accountability.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r3.anchor: وعلمه بأن الذي ناداه هو الله تعالى حصل له بالضرورة خلقا منه تعالى فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r4.claim: The passive 'he was called' first conceals the caller and then magnifies the summons when Moses is named.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r4.anchor: ولما كان في الإبهام ثم تعيين تشويق ثم تعظيم

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.claim: It is said that God called to Moses from a tree in the valley.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.anchor: It is said that in the valley God called to Moses from a tree (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.claim: One interpretation takes the referent to be the tree from which God called Moses.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.anchor: It thus refers to the tree (JJ) or, alternately,

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.speaker: IK, R, Ṭ, Bg, R
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies it with the fire Moses saw, which consumed the tree.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.anchor: to the fire that Moses perceived (see v. 10; IK, R, Ṭ) and which consumed the tree (Bg, R)

TAB-FULL:v16p22/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r2.claim: As Moses approached, the fire withdrew; when he turned back it came closer, and he felt afraid.
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r2.anchor: فلما دنا استأخرت عنه، فلما رأى استئخارها رجع عنها، وأوجس في نفسه منها خيفة

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.claim: Moses knew with certainty that his Lord spoke to him: in revelation the addressee apprehends no other speaker, consistent with the Quran's account of divine communication.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.anchor: فهم من ذلك فهم يقين أن الذي يكلمه هو ربه والكلام كلامه وذلك أنه كان وحيا منه تعالى

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.claim: A prophet's first reception of prophecy or mission is immediate and certain; needing rational proof would make it acquired inference rather than reception from the unseen.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.anchor: ولو افتقر إلى شيء من ذلك كان اكتسابا بواسطة القوة النظرية لا تلقيا من الغيب من غير توسط واسطة

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.claim: Other passages place a veil or intermediary in Moses' call; this is compatible with revelation, since the message is experienced as God's when attention passes over the unseen mediator.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.anchor: فإن التفت إلى الواسطة التي تحمل الكلام واحتجب بها عنه تعالى كان الكلام رسالة أرسل إليه بملك مثلا

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r1.claim: The passive 'he was called' omits the agent with a subtle effect and hints that the sign appeared to Moses suddenly.
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r1.anchor: حيث طوي ذكر الفاعل ولم يقل ناديناه أو ناداه الله من اللطف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses approached the fire, saw it in a jujube tree, and marveled at the bright fire amid intense green: the fire did not spoil the tree and its water did not dim the fire; then he heard a call from the tree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r1.anchor: لما توجه نحو النار فإذا النار في شجرة عناب، فوقف متعجبا من حسن ضوء تلك النار، وشدة خضرة تلك الشجرة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.claim: Qatāda says Moses' two sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey; Moses removed them and approached.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: كانتا من جلد حمار ميت. فخلعهما ثم أتى.

SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.claim: Moses recognized God's call as it enveloped every hair from every direction; awe and majesty confirmed it, and the divine self-identification left him stunned and annihilated. God alone bears and answers His address; Moses is its intermediary locus.
SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : قيل لموسى عليه السلام : كيف عرفت أن النداء هو نداء الحق ؟ فقال : لأني أقياني وشملني

SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r1.claim: The implied subject of the passive verb نودي is Moses.

SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r2.claim: An alternative takes the implied subject to be the verbal noun, meaning 'the call was called'; the author calls this weak.
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r2.anchor: وقيل: ضمير المصدر أي: نودي النداء. وهو ضعيف،

SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r3.claim: The clause يا موسى cannot be the passive verb's subject because a clause cannot serve as a subject.
SAMIN-DURR:20:11/r3.anchor: ومنعوا أن يكون القائم مقامه الجملة من " يا موسى "؛ لأن الجملة لا تكون فاعلا.

ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n8/r1.claim: Asad notes that the passive wording literally means “he was called.”

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.claim: Taha uses atyan more than fifteen times and maji four; Naml uses maji eight times and atyan thirteen, fitting their respective verb choices here.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.anchor: تكرر لفظ الإتيان أكثر من 15 مرة والمجيء 4 مرات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r1.claim: In a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, the fire was in a verdant, luxuriant jujube tree.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r1.anchor: وكانت كما في بعض الروايات عن ابن عباس في شجرة عناب خضراء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd says the fire was in a samura tree.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود : كانت في سمرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r3.claim: Another reported location is an awsj tree.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r4.speaker: وهب بن منية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r4.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih narrates that Moses saw a huge fire in a very green al-ʿalīq tree: it grew without burning the tree, repeatedly approached and withdrew as he tried to take a flame, then became a brilliant pillar reaching skyward. Moses feared and wondered at it; the extraordinary scene culminated in angelic praise and calm. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166#2/r4.anchor: وأخرج الإمام أحمد في الزهد وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن وهب ابن منية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r1.speaker: قالوا
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r1.claim: One fourfold scheme says worldly fire eats but does not drink, green-tree fire drinks but does not eat, Hellfire does both, and Moses’s fire does neither.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r1.anchor: وقالوا : النار أربعة أصناف صنف يأكل ولا يشرب وهي نار الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r2.speaker: قالوا
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r2.claim: A second scheme classifies fires by light and burning: worldly fire has both, tree fire neither, Hellfire burns without light, and Moses’s fire shines without burning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r2.anchor: وقالوا أيضا هي أربع أنواع نوع له نور وإحراق وهي نار الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r3.claim: Another view, reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, is that this was not fire but light from God’s light; the verse calls it fire because that is how Moses perceived it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r3.anchor: بل قال بعضهم : إنها لم تكن نارا بل هي نور من نور الرب تبارك وتعالى وروي هذا عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān favors interpreting the phenomenon as light rather than actual fire; al-Māwardī also adopts this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r4.anchor: واستظهر ذلك أبو حيان واليه ذهب الماوردي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says it was fire itself and one of God’s veils.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير هي النار بعينها وهي إحدى حجب الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r6.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r6.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī transmits the Prophet’s statement that God’s veil is fire and that uncovering it would burn every creature reached by the radiance of His face; al-Baghawī cites it and al-Khāzin says Muslim recorded it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r6.anchor: واستدل له نما روى عن أبى موسى الأشعرى عن النبى ( صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ) قال : حجابه النار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r7.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r7.claim: Some Muʿtazilites use the verse’s apparent immediate call to reject reports that an interval passed between Moses’s arrival and the call.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r7.anchor: بذلك رد بعض المعتزلة الأخبار السابقة الدالة على تخلل زمان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī replies that an interval of the reported kind does not undermine those accounts.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r8.anchor: وانت تعلم أن تخلل مثل ذلك الزمان مما لا يضر في مثل ما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r9.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r9.claim: Some Muʿtazilites deny that a miracle could appear when Moses reached the fire before his prophetic commission, unless it were a miracle for another prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r9.anchor: وزعم أيضا امتناع تحقق ظهور الخارق عند مجيئه النار قبل أن ينبأ إلا أن يكون ذلك معجزة لغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī classifies the pre-prophetic marvel as irhāṣ, a precursor miracle that the Muʿtazilites reject.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r10.anchor: وعندنا أن ذلك من الارهاص الذي ينكره المعتزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r11.claim: The apparent passive-subject pronoun refers to Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن القائم مقام فاعل ( نودى ) ضمير موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r12.claim: Another grammatical proposal takes the passive subject as a verbal noun: the calling occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r12.anchor: وقيل : ضمير المصدر أي نودي النداء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r13.claim: A third proposal makes the quoted words يا موسى the subject by treating the call as including speech and taking that wording as the intended message.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r14.speaker: الكوفيون
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r14.claim: The Kūfans treat calling as equivalent to saying; the Basrans instead posit an omitted saying verb, so the meaning is that Moses was called and told يا موسى.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167/r14.anchor: وفي البحر مذهب الكوفيين معاملة النداء معاملة القول ومذهب البصريين اضمار القول في مثل هذه الآية

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.claim: When Moses reached the fire, he found a white flame burning in a green tree and was called by name.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r1.anchor: أي النار وجد نارا بيضاء تتقد في شجرة خضراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the fire; when Moses came to it, he was called.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى فلما أتاها يعني النار نودي يا موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.claim: Moses came to the fire and drew near to it, whereupon he was called by name.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.anchor: أي: النار واقترب (1) منها، {نودي يا موسى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.claim: The call to Moses is compared with the account of his being called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.anchor: وفي الآية الأخرى: {نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله} [القصص: 30]

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.claim: Abu ʿAmr and Ibn Kathir read أني with fatḥ, meaning Moses was called with the words that I am your Lord; the others read kasr, meaning he was called, O Moses, or treating the call as speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير ( أني ) بالفتح ، أي : نودي بأني { أنا ربك } وكسر الباقون ،

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r1.claim: The thing Moses came to was the fire, which was light.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r2.claim: One view is that God addressed Moses directly and alone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r2.anchor: وفي هذا النداء قولان : أحدهما : أنه تفرد بندائه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r3.claim: Another view says God made the light speak with a call from His inseparable light, calming Moses so he could bear God's command.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r3.anchor: أن الله أنطق النور بهذا النداء فكان من نوره الذي لا ينفصل عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r1.claim: Moses found white fire blazing through a green tree, either a jujube or an osage tree.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r1.anchor: أي النار وجد نارا بيضاء تتوقد في شجرة خضراء من اسفلها إلى أعلاها وكانت شجرة العناب أو العوسج

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r2.claim: He found no one by the fire; a report says it moved away when he approached and neared him when he stopped seeking it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r2.anchor: ولم يجد عندها أحد أو روى انه كلما طلبها بعدت عنه فاذا تركها قربت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#4/r3.anchor: فبم منه ﴿ نودي ﴾ موسى ﴿ يا موسى ﴿

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.claim: Qabas is a flame from fire, and miqbās is likewise a firebrand or fire-taking implement.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.anchor: والقبس شعلة من نار، وكذلك المقباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r3.claim: Qabistu and iqtibās can refer to taking fire; iqtibās can also mean acquiring knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r3.anchor: وكذلك اقتبست منه نارا، واقتبست منه علما أيضا أي استفدته،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.speaker: اليزيدي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.claim: Al-Yazīdī distinguishes aqbastu someone knowledge from qabastu him fire; aqbastu is used when seeking knowledge for someone.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.anchor: قال اليزيدي: أقبست الرجل علما وقبسته نارا فإن كنت طلبتها له قلت أقبسته

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī permits aqbastuhu for either fire or knowledge; qabastuhu also applies to both.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.anchor: وقال الكسائي: أقبسته نارا أو علما سواء. وقبسته أيضا فيهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r6.claim: Hudā here means hādiyan, a guide.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.claim: The pronoun in أتاها refers to the fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فلمآ أتاها } يعني النار

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.claim: Moses was called from the tree's direction and vicinity, as in Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.anchor: أي من الشجرة كما في سورة «القصص» أي من جهتها وناحيتها

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses saw a green tree encircled from base to top by brilliantly burning white fire, with no person nearby; neither the fire dimmed the tree nor the tree's water dimmed the fire.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : رأى شجرة خضراء

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r2.claim: Moses heard the angels glorifying God, saw a light too intense for eyes, covered his eyes, and was overcome with fear and astonishment before calm was sent upon him.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r2.anchor: فسمع تسبيح الملائكة ورأى نورا عظيما تكل الأبصار عنه فوضع يديه على عينيه وخاف وبهت

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r3.speaker: قالوا
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r3.claim: The tree is identified variously as a green samura, an ʿawsaja, a blackberry-like thorn tree, or a jujube; these trees contain no fire unlike other trees.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r3.anchor: وكانت الشجرة سمرة خضراء أو عوسجة أو عليقا أو شجرة العناب وهي شجرة لا نار فيها

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r4.speaker: قالوا
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r4.claim: One four-part classification says worldly fire eats but does not drink, green-tree fire drinks but does not eat, Hellfire both eats and drinks, and Moses' fire neither eats nor drinks.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r4.anchor: قالوا : النار أربعة أصناف : صنف يأكل ولا يشرب

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r5.speaker: قالوا
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r5.claim: A second classification distinguishes fire with burning but no light (Hell), light without burning (Moses), both (worldly fire), and neither (trees).
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r5.anchor: وقالوا أيضا هي أربعة أنواع : نوع له إحراق بلا نور

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.claim: In the inward reading, light signifies love and fire signifies ardent love; when Moses' love and longing were full, the essential light appeared in the form of attribute-fire, burned away his selfhood, and brought single-hearted orientation.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.anchor: يقول الفقير : النور للمحبة والنار للعشق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r6.claim: The passive “he was called” heightens anticipation by withholding the caller’s identity; “I am your Lord” then reveals it and depicts the unknown voice Moses heard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r6.anchor: بني فعل النداء للمجهول زيادة في التشويق إلى استطلاع القصة ، فإبهام المنادي يشوق سامع الآية
